title: Clocked Simulation of Boolean Decrement
statement: Let $k$ be a natural number, let $\Gamma,S,Q$ be types with decidable equality on $\Gamma$, let $x$ be a finite word over $\Gamma$, let $e$ inject the Boolean alphabet into $\Gamma$, let $H$ be a machine with $k+1$ work tapes, and let $\rho$ inject the flagged phases into its state set $Q$. Suppose that for every phase other than a done phase, every input symbol and every tuple of work-tape symbols, the transition of $H$ at the corresponding state equals the transition obtained by embedding Boolean decrement on the last tape, encoding symbols by $e$, and renaming phases by $\rho$. Let $c$ be a configuration with $k$ work tapes on input $x$, let $w$ be a finite Boolean word, and let $ct:\mathbb Z\to\mathrm{Option}(\Gamma)$ and $cp\in\mathbb Z$ satisfy that, for each $p$ with $-1\le p\le |w|$, $ct(cp+p)$ equals the tape encoding of $w$ at offset $p$. Starting with $c$ extended by this tape, its head at $cp$, and state $\rho(run)$, after $2r+2$ steps, where $r$ is the number of initial false bits of $w$, the state is $\rho(done((decFixed(w)).isSome))$, the original configuration components remain those of $c$, and the added tape is patched with $e$ applied to the decremented word when decrement is defined and otherwise to the all-true word of length $|w|$. Before that time the machine is never in a done state. At every time up to and including $2r+2$, the configuration consists of $c$ with its current state and added tape, the added head lies in $[cp-1,cp+|w|]$, and its state is the image under $\rho$ of an optional flagged phase.

replaced:
Let $k$ be a natural number, let $\Gamma$, $S$, and $Q$ be types, and let $\Gamma$ have
decidable equality. Let $x$ be a finite word over $\Gamma$, let $e$ be an injection from
the Boolean alphabet into $\Gamma$, and let $H$ be a deterministic machine with $k+1$
work tapes, alphabet $\Gamma$, and state set $Q$. Let $\rho$ inject the flagged
computation phases into $Q$. Suppose that whenever a phase is not a live exit phase, the
transition of $H$ at the corresponding state agrees, for every input symbol and every
tuple of work-tape symbols, with the transition obtained by running Boolean decrement on
the last tape, encoding symbols by $e$, and renaming phases by $\rho$. Let $c$ be a
configuration with $k$ work tapes on input $x$, let $w$ be a finite Boolean word, and
let $ct:\mathbb Z\to\mathrm{Option}(\Gamma)$ and $cp\in\mathbb Z$. Assume that for every
integer $p$ with $-1\le p\le |w|$, the tape $ct$ at position $cp+p$ agrees with the tape
storing the encoded word $e(w)$ from position $0$. Starting from the configuration
formed by adjoining this tape to $c$ with head at $cp$ and state $\rho(\mathrm{run})$,
after $2r+2$ steps, where $r$ is the number of initial false bits of $w$, the state is
$\rho(\mathrm{done}(b))$, with $b$ true exactly when Boolean decrement of $w$ is
defined. The original configuration components remain those of $c$, and the added tape
agrees with $ct$ outside the cells from $cp$ through $cp+|w|-1$; on those cells it
stores the encoded decremented word when decrement is defined, and otherwise stores the
encoding of the all-true word of length $|w|$. No earlier step is in a live exit state.
At every step up to and including step $2r+2$, the configuration consists of $c$
together with its current state and added tape, the added tape head lies in the interval
$[cp-1,cp+|w|]$, and the state is the image under $\rho$ of an optional flagged phase.
